note: Starting points, not an inventory. Every organisation is different: take what fits, change the wording, and delete the rest. Scores are a first guess to argue with, not an answer. The controls shown against each one are the Annex A controls that usually treat it.

items.name: Key personnel / single points of knowledge

items.title: Unpatched critical vulnerability exploited
items.description: A known flaw in an internet-facing system is not patched in time and is exploited before anyone notices it was outstanding.

items.title: Staff credentials taken by phishing
items.description: An employee enters their password and one-time code on a convincing fake sign-in page, handing an attacker a working session.

items.title: Ransomware encrypts servers and backups
items.description: Ransomware spreads to file servers and reaches the backups as well, so recovery takes weeks instead of hours.

items.title: Supplier breach exposes your information
items.description: A supplier holding or processing your data is compromised, and your customers are affected by an incident that never touched your network.

items.title: Cloud storage or service left publicly accessible
items.description: A misconfiguration exposes a storage bucket, database or admin console to the internet, usually discovered by somebody outside the organisation.

items.title: Privileged administrator misuses their access
items.description: Someone with unrestricted rights reads, changes or deletes what they should not, and without logging nobody can prove what happened.

items.title: Leaver keeps access after departure
items.description: Accounts and equipment are not taken back when someone leaves, so a former employee or contractor still has a working way in.

items.title: Malware spreads across a flat network
items.description: An infection on one laptop reaches servers and other offices because the network is not divided, turning one machine into an organisation-wide incident.

items.title: Vulnerable third-party library shipped to production
items.description: An open-source component with a known flaw is built into an application because nothing checks what the software is made of.

items.title: Sensitive data leaves by email or removable media
items.description: A member of staff sends or copies confidential information out of the organisation, whether by mistake or on purpose.

items.title: Intrusion goes undetected for months
items.description: An attacker is inside the network but nothing raises an alarm, and logs from different systems cannot be lined up to work out what happened.

items.title: Recovery fails when it is actually needed
items.description: Recovery plans exist on paper but have never been tested, and the systems do not come back when the main site or cloud region is lost.

items.title: Expired certificate takes a service down
items.description: Nobody owns a certificate or is warned before it lapses, and a public service stops working for reasons that look like an attack.

items.title: Untested change breaks production
items.description: A change is made straight in the live environment without testing or a way back, causing an outage. More outages come from changes than from attackers.

items.title: Systems in use that nobody knows about
items.description: Teams buy or build their own tools, so information sits outside every control the organisation believes it has.

items.title: Information security has no clear owner or backing
items.description: Responsibility is spread across roles with nobody accountable and no support from management, so nothing improves between audits.

items.title: Incident handled badly because nobody knows the plan
items.description: When something goes wrong, people do not know who to call or what to do first, so the damage grows while roles are argued over.

items.title: Breach not reported to authorities in time
items.description: A personal data breach is not recognised or escalated quickly enough, and the deadline to tell the regulator or the people affected is missed.

items.title: Evidence destroyed while responding to an incident
items.description: In the rush to restore service, logs are overwritten and machines rebuilt, so the cause cannot be proved and legal action or an insurance claim fails.

items.title: The same incident keeps happening
items.description: Incidents are closed as soon as service is back, nobody looks for the cause, and the same weakness is exploited again months later.

items.title: Laptop lost or stolen with unencrypted data
items.description: A laptop or phone is left on a train or taken from a car, and the information on it is readable by whoever has it.

items.title: Home working exposes confidential information
items.description: People work from home or in public places on shared devices and open screens, with papers left out and conversations overheard.

items.title: Person hired on false credentials given access
items.description: Someone joins with a faked history or undisclosed conflicts, and receives access to sensitive information before any checks are done.

items.title: Staff mishandle information because nothing says how sensitive it is
items.description: Documents and data carry no classification or label, so confidential material is shared, printed and stored like everything else.

items.title: Staff ignore security rules because nothing happens when they do
items.description: Rules are published but breaking them has no consequence, so shortcuts become normal practice and the policy is ignored.

items.title: Unauthorised person gets into the office or server room
items.description: Someone gets in by following staff through a door, using an old badge or walking in unescorted, and reaches equipment or papers.

items.title: Fire, flood or power loss in the server room
items.description: Equipment in a poorly protected room is damaged by water, heat or an electrical fault, or stops when the power fails.

items.title: Equipment or cabling fails for lack of care
items.description: Unmaintained equipment breaks down and exposed cabling is damaged or tapped, taking systems down without warning.

items.title: Old equipment disposed of with data still on it
items.description: Laptops, disks and phones are sold, recycled or thrown away without being wiped, and the information on them is recovered by someone else.

items.title: Real customer data exposed in test environments
items.description: Copies of live data are used for development and testing, where access is loose and nobody treats it as sensitive.

items.title: Source code or secrets stolen from the repository
items.description: Source code, passwords or keys in a code repository are copied by someone who should not have access, exposing products and systems.

items.title: An audit or test disrupts live systems
items.description: A vulnerability scan, penetration test or audit query runs against production without planning, and slows or stops a live service.

items.title: Unlicensed software or copied material in use
items.description: Software, fonts, images or documents are used without the right licence, leading to fines, legal claims or forced removal.

items.title: Warnings about new threats not acted on
items.description: Alerts from suppliers, industry groups or authorities about an active threat arrive, but nobody reads them or checks whether they apply.

items.title: Security left out of new projects
items.description: Projects and new systems are designed and bought without security requirements, so weaknesses are built in and costly to fix later.

items.title: Systems run out of capacity at peak times
items.description: Storage, processing or network capacity is not watched, and a service slows or fails at the busiest moment.

items.title: Controls exist on paper but nobody checks they work
items.description: Policies and procedures are written but never independently reviewed, so gaps are only found by an external auditor or an attacker.

items.title: Key tasks only one person knows how to do
items.description: Backups, restores and admin tasks are done from memory by one person, and nobody else can do them when that person is away or leaves.

items.title: Access granted without approval and never reviewed
items.description: People collect access as they move between roles because requests are not approved and nobody reviews who has what.

items.title: Weak or shared passwords
items.description: Shared accounts, default passwords and simple passwords reused across systems let one leaked password open many doors.

items.title: Legal or contractual requirement missed
items.description: A law, regulation or customer contract sets a security or privacy obligation that nobody has listed, and it is breached without anyone knowing.

items.title: Records lost or destroyed too early
items.description: Records that must be kept for legal or business reasons are deleted, damaged or cannot be found when a regulator or court asks for them.

items.title: Supplier changes its service without telling you
items.description: A cloud or managed service provider changes how its service works, where data is held or who subcontracts it, and nobody reviews the effect.

items.title: Harmful websites and downloads reach staff
items.description: Staff browse to malicious or compromised websites and download infected files, because nothing filters where they can go.

items.title: Ransomware Disrupting Clinical Operations
items.description: Ransomware encrypts hospital systems and clinical applications, forcing a shift to manual processes and delaying or cancelling patient procedures.

items.title: Unsupported Legacy Medical Devices
items.description: Medical devices such as infusion pumps and imaging systems run outdated, unpatchable software, giving attackers a stable foothold inside clinical networks.

items.title: Unauthorized Staff Access to Patient Records
items.description: Employees browse or share patient records outside their care responsibilities, breaching patient confidentiality and triggering regulatory reporting obligations.

items.title: Tampering with Networked Medical Devices
items.description: An attacker on the clinical network alters settings on a networked medical device, risking incorrect dosing or device malfunction that directly endangers patients.

items.title: Electronic Health Record (EHR) Downtime
items.description: The EHR system becomes unavailable during patient care, leaving clinicians without access to allergies, medication history or care plans.

items.title: Breach at a Medical Billing or Transcription Vendor
items.description: A third-party billing or transcription vendor is breached, exposing patient and payment data the organisation shared with them.

items.title: Interception of Telehealth Sessions
items.description: Telehealth consultations or their recordings are intercepted or accessed without authorization, exposing sensitive clinical conversations.

items.title: Theft of Clinical Research Data
items.description: Confidential clinical trial or research data is accessed or exfiltrated by unauthorized parties, undermining trial integrity and competitive position.

items.title: Non-Compliance with Health Data Privacy Regulations
items.description: Patient data is processed without meeting applicable health-privacy regulatory requirements, exposing the organisation to fines and mandatory breach notification.

items.title: Hospital IoT as a Network Entry Point
items.description: Connected hospital equipment (infusion pumps, building systems, patient monitors) with weak security is used by an attacker as an entry point into the wider network.

items.title: Unauthorized Alteration of Patient Records
items.description: A user with write access to the EHR system alters a patient record — such as an allergy, medication or dosage entry — without authorization, creating a direct risk to patient safety.

items.title: Medical Identity Theft
items.description: Stolen patient identity information is used to fraudulently obtain medical treatment, prescriptions or insurance payouts under the victim's name.

items.title: Business Email Compromise / Wire Fraud
items.description: Attackers impersonate executives or vendors to trick finance staff into redirecting a wire transfer, resulting in direct financial loss.

items.title: Core Banking or Trading System Outage
items.description: A failure or attack on core banking or trading systems halts customer transactions, triggering financial loss and regulatory scrutiny.

items.title: Cardholder Data Breach
items.description: Payment card data held or processed by the organisation is exposed, triggering PCI DSS non-compliance findings and card-scheme penalties.

items.title: Large-Scale Customer Account Takeover
items.description: Credential-stuffing attacks compromise customer accounts at scale, resulting in fraudulent transactions and reimbursement costs.

items.title: Insider Misuse of Financial Data
items.description: An employee with privileged access to financial systems misuses customer or market data for personal gain, including potential insider trading.

items.title: Gaps in Anti-Money-Laundering Screening
items.description: Weaknesses in transaction monitoring or customer screening allow money-laundering activity to pass undetected, creating regulatory and criminal exposure.

items.title: Abuse of Open Banking APIs
items.description: Poorly secured open-banking APIs are exploited to scrape customer data or perform unauthorized transactions.

items.title: Physical Skimming at ATMs or POS Terminals
items.description: Card-skimming devices installed on ATMs or point-of-sale terminals capture customer card data for later fraud.

items.title: Tampering with Financial Reporting Data
items.description: Financial records are altered without authorization, undermining the integrity of statutory financial reporting.

items.title: Regulatory Non-Compliance Fines
items.description: The organisation fails to meet financial-sector regulatory requirements, resulting in fines, sanctions or licence restrictions.

items.title: Synthetic Identity Fraud at Onboarding
items.description: Criminals create accounts using fabricated or stolen-and-blended identity details that pass basic verification, enabling fraud that is difficult to trace to a real victim.

items.title: Errors in Automated Credit or Trading Decision Models
items.description: Flaws or drift in automated credit-scoring or trading algorithms produce incorrect decisions, causing financial loss or unfair customer outcomes and regulatory scrutiny.

items.title: OT/ICS Compromise Halting Production
items.description: An attacker gains access to industrial control systems on the plant floor, forcing an emergency production shutdown.

items.title: IT-to-OT Network Pivot
items.description: An attacker who compromises office IT systems pivots across an insufficiently segmented network into operational technology.

items.title: Unpatchable Legacy PLCs and SCADA Systems
items.description: Programmable logic controllers and SCADA systems run outdated firmware that cannot be patched without a full production outage.

items.title: Tampering with Safety Instrumented Systems
items.description: An attacker alters settings on a safety system, creating a risk of physical harm to workers or equipment damage.

items.title: Theft of Product Designs and Formulas
items.description: CAD files, product formulas or process documentation are exfiltrated, giving competitors or counterfeiters access to proprietary designs.

items.title: Key Supplier Breach Halting Material Supply
items.description: A critical raw-material or component supplier suffers an outage or breach, interrupting the organisation's production schedule.

items.title: Counterfeit Components Entering Production
items.description: Counterfeit or substandard components enter the supply chain undetected, creating product quality and safety risks.

items.title: Ransomware on ERP/MES Systems
items.description: Ransomware encrypts enterprise resource planning or manufacturing execution systems, halting scheduling, shipping and invoicing.

items.title: Falsification of Quality or Test Records
items.description: Quality assurance or compliance test records are altered to conceal defects, risking product recalls and regulatory action.

items.title: Unauthorized Physical Access to Production Areas
items.description: Individuals without authorization gain physical access to production floors, risking sabotage, theft or safety incidents.

items.title: Uncontrolled Third-Party Remote Access to OT Systems
items.description: External maintenance vendors keep persistent or poorly monitored remote-access connections into plant equipment, providing an unmonitored entry point into operational technology.

items.title: Nation-State Targeted Intrusion
items.description: A state-sponsored threat actor conducts a sustained campaign against government systems to steal sensitive information or disrupt services.

items.title: Large-Scale Citizen Data Registry Breach
items.description: A breach of a citizen records system exposes personal data for a large portion of the population, triggering mass notification obligations.

items.title: Leakage of Classified or Sensitive Information
items.description: An insider or mishandling incident results in classified or sensitive government information being disclosed outside authorized channels.

items.title: Disruption of Critical Public Services
items.description: An attack or system failure disrupts a critical public service (e.g. benefits, permits, emergency systems), affecting citizens directly.

items.title: Legacy Systems Supporting Essential Services
items.description: Core government services run on ageing, unsupported systems that are increasingly difficult to secure or maintain.

items.title: Uncontrolled Cross-Agency Data Sharing
items.description: Citizen data is shared between agencies without consistent controls, increasing the risk of misuse or unauthorized secondary use.

items.title: Excessive Contractor Access to Sensitive Systems
items.description: External contractors retain broad access to sensitive government systems beyond what their engagement requires.

items.title: Website Defacement or Disinformation
items.description: A public-facing government website is defaced or used to spread disinformation, damaging public trust in official communications.

items.title: Records Management and Freedom-of-Information Failures
items.description: Poor records management results in the organisation being unable to meet statutory records-retention or freedom-of-information obligations.

items.title: Procurement Fraud via System Manipulation
items.description: Procurement or payment systems are manipulated to divert public funds to fraudulent suppliers.

items.title: Unauthorized Staff Lookups of Citizen Records
items.description: Government employees access citizen records out of curiosity or for personal reasons without a legitimate case-related need, breaching citizens' privacy.

items.title: Ransomware Closing School or Campus Operations
items.description: Ransomware encrypts administrative and learning systems, forcing campus closures or a shift to manual operations.

items.title: Breach of Student Data, Including Minors
items.description: Student records, including data belonging to children, are exposed, creating heightened legal and reputational consequences.

items.title: Uncontrolled Personal Devices on Campus Networks
items.description: Thousands of unmanaged student and staff devices connect to campus networks, creating a large and inconsistent attack surface.

items.title: Tampering with Grades or Examination Records
items.description: A student or staff member gains unauthorized access to alter grades or examination results.

items.title: Theft of Research Data by External Actors
items.description: State-linked or competitive actors target university research systems to steal valuable research data or intellectual property.

items.title: EdTech / Learning Platform Vendor Breach
items.description: A third-party learning platform or EdTech vendor is breached, exposing student data shared with them.

items.title: Payroll-Redirect Phishing Against Staff
items.description: Phishing emails trick payroll or HR staff into redirecting employee salary payments to attacker-controlled accounts.

items.title: Open Campus Wi-Fi as an Attack Surface
items.description: Open or weakly secured campus wireless networks are used to intercept traffic or attack connected devices.

items.title: Online Examination Fraud
items.description: Weaknesses in online exam platforms allow impersonation, unauthorized assistance or answer leakage during remote assessments.

items.title: Unauthorized Access to Child-Safeguarding Records
items.description: Sensitive child-welfare or safeguarding records are accessed by staff without a legitimate need, breaching duty-of-care obligations.

items.title: Remote Exploitation of Connected Vehicles
items.description: A vulnerability in a vehicle's connected systems is exploited remotely, potentially allowing unauthorized control of vehicle functions.

items.title: Compromised Over-the-Air Update Channel
items.description: An attacker compromises the over-the-air update mechanism, allowing malicious firmware to be pushed to the vehicle fleet.

items.title: Factory OT Compromise Halting Assembly
items.description: Industrial control systems on the vehicle assembly line are compromised, forcing a production stoppage.

items.title: Vehicle Telematics Privacy Breach
items.description: Location and driving-behaviour data collected via vehicle telematics is exposed or misused, breaching customer privacy expectations.

items.title: Key-Fob Relay Attacks Enabling Vehicle Theft
items.description: Attackers use relay devices to capture and replay key-fob signals, allowing a vehicle to be unlocked and stolen without the physical key.

items.title: Infotainment System as a Pivot to Vehicle Controls
items.description: A vulnerability in the infotainment system is used to pivot into safety-critical vehicle control networks (e.g. CAN bus).

items.title: Compromised Component or Software from a Supplier
items.description: A tier-1 or tier-2 supplier delivers a component or embedded software containing a vulnerability or malicious code.

items.title: Data or Model Poisoning in Autonomous Driving Systems
items.description: Training data or models used in driver-assistance or autonomous-driving features are manipulated, degrading safety-critical decision-making.

items.title: Dealer Network Data Breach
items.description: A breach at a dealership exposes customer, finance or vehicle-ownership data shared through the dealer network.

items.title: Non-Compliance with Automotive Cybersecurity Regulations
items.description: The organisation fails to meet automotive cybersecurity regulatory requirements (e.g. UNECE R155 / ISO 21434), risking type-approval or market-access loss.

items.title: Attacks on EV Charging Infrastructure and Fleet Cloud Backend
items.description: Vulnerabilities in electric-vehicle charging stations or the fleet management cloud backend are exploited to disrupt charging services, commit payment fraud, or pivot into connected-vehicle systems.
